q: About _____ of the mass of the Earth's crust consists of oxygen.
e: About 50% of the mass of the Earth's crust consists of oxygen.

q: The free element of oxygen accounts for _____ of the volume of the atmosphere.
e: The free element accounts for 21% of the volume of the atmosphere.

q: In the laboratory, oxygen gas can be prepared by using an environmentally friendly liquid _____ of appropriate strength.
e: Oxygen gas can be prepared by using an environmentally friendly liquid hydrogen peroxide of appropriate strength.

q: In the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide, _____ is used as a catalyst to speed up the chemical reaction.
e: Manganese(IV) oxide is used as a catalyst to speed up the chemical reaction.

q: Oxygen gas is collected by the _____ of water.
e: Oxygen gas is collected by the downward displacement of water.

q: The chemical equation for the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide is _____.
e: The reaction is $2H_2O_2(aq) \xrightarrow{MnO_2} 2H_2O(l) + O_2(g)$.

q: Oxygen is a colourless gas, without taste or smell, and is only _____ soluble in water.
e: Oxygen is only slightly soluble in water.

q: Oxygen will not burn, however, it _____ combustion.
e: Oxygen will not burn, however, it supports combustion.

q: Oxygen rekindles any glowing thing (splinter) with a _____.
e: It rekindles any glowing thing (splinter) with a bright flame.

q: When magnesium burns in oxygen from air, it leaves a white powder residue which is _____.
e: This residue is magnesium oxide (MgO).

q: The chemical equation for the burning of magnesium ribbon in oxygen is _____.
e: The equation is $2Mg(s) + O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2MgO(s)$.

q: Iron slowly becomes oxidised in the presence of air and water to form hydrated iron(III) oxide, which is commonly known as _____.
e: Iron has become rusted, forming hydrated iron(III) oxide.

q: Non-metals such as phosphorus, sulphur and carbon react with oxygen forming _____.
e: Non-metals react with oxygen forming oxides.

q: Red phosphorus burns in oxygen giving off white fumes which consist of _____.
e: The white fumes consist of oxides of phosphorus.

q: An acidic oxide is an oxide of _____.
e: An acidic oxide is an oxide of non-metal.

q: An acidic oxide reacts with basic oxides to give _____ only.
e: It reacts with basic oxides to give salts in only.

q: Acidic oxides react with alkali solutions to give _____.
e: Acidic oxides react with alkali solutions to give salts and water.

q: The test for carbon dioxide involves passing it into calcium hydroxide solution, which turns milky due to the formation of _____.
e: Carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide to form calcium carbonate and water.

q: Among the following, the insoluble acidic oxide is _____.
e: $SiO_2$ is an insoluble oxide, while $CO_2$ and $SO_3$ are soluble.

q: Soluble acidic oxides dissolve in water to form acidic solutions. These solutions turn blue litmus _____.
e: These solutions turn blue litmus red.

q: A basic oxide is an oxide of _____.
e: A basic oxide is an oxide of metal.

q: A basic oxide reacts with an acid to produce _____.
e: A basic oxide reacts with an acid to produce a salt and water only.

q: Among the following, the insoluble basic oxide is _____.
e: $MgO$, $CuO$ and $Ag_2O$ are insoluble basic oxides, while $Na_2O$ and $K_2O$ are soluble.

q: Some basic oxides react with water forming hydroxide solutions (alkalis). These solutions turn red litmus _____.
e: These solutions turn red litmus blue.

q: An amphoteric oxide is a metallic oxide which possesses _____.
e: An amphoteric oxide possesses both basic and acidic properties.

q: An amphoteric oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis to form _____.
e: It reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salt and water.

q: Which of the following is an example of an amphoteric oxide?
e: $ZnO$, $Al_2O_3$ and $PbO$ are examples of amphoteric oxides.

q: A neutral oxide is an oxide which shows _____.
e: The neutral oxide shows neither basic nor acidic character.

q: Which of the following is an example of a neutral oxide?
e: $CO$ and $N_2O$ are examples of neutral oxides.

q: Peroxides are oxides that react with an acid to give salt and _____.
e: Peroxides react with an acid to give salt and hydrogen peroxide.

q: Which of the following is an example of a peroxide?
e: $BaO_2$ and $Na_2O_2$ are peroxides. $PbO_2$ and $MnO_2$ are not.

q: $PbO_2$, $MnO_2$ and $NO_2$ are not peroxides because they _____.
a: do not give hydrogen peroxides on reaction with acids
e: They do not give hydrogen peroxides on reaction with acids.

q: A compound oxide is an oxide, formed by the combination of two different oxides of the _____.
e: A compound oxide is formed by the combination of two different oxides of the same element.

q: Which of the following is an example of a compound oxide?
e: $Pb_3O_4$, $Mn_3O_4$ and $Fe_3O_4$ are compound oxides.

q: $Pb_3O_4$ can be written as di-lead(II) lead(IV) oxide or _____.
e: $Pb_3O_4$ can be written as di-lead(II) lead(IV) oxide or red lead oxide.

q: When red lead oxide reacts with dilute nitric acid, only _____ reacts with the acid to form lead(II) nitrate.
e: Lead(II) oxide only reacts with the acid to form lead(II) nitrate.

q: In living organisms, the oxygen intake is used for the breakdown of the _____ molecules to produce energy.
e: Oxygen intake is used for the breakdown of the glucose molecules to produce energy.

q: Liquid oxygen is carried on rockets to _____.
e: Liquid oxygen is carried on rockets to support the fuel burns.

q: Which oxide is used in fire extinguishers?
e: $CO_2$ is used in fire extinguishers.

q: Which oxide is used as a bleaching agent?
e: $SO_2$ is used as a bleaching agent.

q: Carbon is found in nature as diamond and _____.
e: Carbon is found in nature as diamond and graphite.

q: Fullerene and graphene are _____ carbon.
e: Fullerene and graphene are synthetic carbon.

q: If an element can exist in more than one form, in the same physical state, it is said to exhibit _____.
e: It is said to exhibit allotropy or polymorphism.

q: The different forms of an element in the same physical state that possess different physical properties are known as _____.
e: They are known as allotropes of that element.

q: Which of the following are allotropes of carbon?
e: Diamond, graphite, fullerene and graphene are allotropes of carbon.

q: In diamond, each carbon atom is surrounded by _____ other carbon atoms.
e: In diamond, each carbon atom is surrounded by four other carbon atoms.

q: Diamond has a giant structure containing millions of carbon atoms in a three dimensional network of strong _____.
e: It contains a three dimensional network of strong carbon-carbon covalent bonds.

q: The melting point of diamond is _____.
e: Diamond has a very high melting point of 3550 °C.

q: Diamond is the _____ among all naturally occurring substances.
e: Diamond is the hardest among all naturally occurring substances.

q: In graphite, each carbon atom is surrounded by _____ other carbon atoms in the same plane.
e: In graphite, each carbon atom is surrounded by three other carbon atoms in the same plane.

q: In graphite, layers of hexagons are weakly bonded to each other through weak forces known as _____.
e: The layers are bonded through weak forces known as van der Waals forces.

q: Due to its layered structure, graphite is soft and has a _____ touch.
e: Graphite is soft and has a soapy touch.

q: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity and heat due to the presence of _____.
e: Due to the presence of free electrons, it is a good conductor of electricity and heat.

q: The melting point of graphite is _____.
e: The melting point of graphite is 3700 °C.

q: Fullerene ($C_{60}$) is an allotrope of carbon in the form of a _____.
a: hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes
e: Fullerene is in the form of a hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes.

q: Spherical fullerenes are also referred to as _____.
e: Spherical fullerenes are also referred to as Bucky balls.

q: Fullerenes have _____ melting and boiling points than diamond and graphite.
e: Fullerenes have lower melting and boiling points than diamond and graphite.

q: Graphene is a _____ of graphite.
e: Graphene is a single layer (monolayer) of graphite.

q: Graphene's crystalline structure is _____.
e: Its crystalline structure is two-dimensional.

q: In proportion to its thickness, graphene is about _____ stronger than the strongest steel.
e: It is about 100 times stronger than the strongest steel.

q: Charcoal is made by heating wood in the _____.
e: Charcoal is made by heating wood in the absence of air.

q: Charcoal has a _____ structure and has many small holes.
e: It has a porous structure and has many small holes.

q: Coke is formed by heating coal in the absence of air and is almost _____.
e: Coke is almost pure carbon.

q: Carbon black (soot) is left as a residue when kerosene is burnt in a _____ amount of air.
e: Carbon black is left when kerosene is burnt in a limited amount of air.

q: When carbon burns in excess air or oxygen, _____ is formed.
e: When carbon burns in excess air or oxygen, carbon dioxide is formed.

q: When carbon burns in a limited amount of air or oxygen, _____ is formed.
e: Carbon monoxide is formed when carbon burns in a limited amount of air or oxygen.

q: Carbon can be used as a _____ in the extraction of some metals.
e: Carbon can be used as a reducing agent in the extraction of some metals.

q: When strongly heated, carbon can reduce the oxides of zinc to zinc and _____.
e: Carbon reduces zinc oxide to zinc and carbon monoxide.

q: Diamond is used for jewellery because of its _____.
e: Diamond is used for jewellery because of its brilliant shine.

q: Powdered graphite is used as a dry lubricant for machine parts which operate at high temperature because graphite is _____.
e: Graphite is non-volatile, making it suitable as a dry lubricant at high temperatures.

q: Fullerene is used in artificial photosynthesis, cosmetics, surface coating of medical devices and _____.
e: Fullerene is used in artificial photosynthesis, cosmetics, surface coating of medical devices and drug delivery system.

q: Graphene is widely used for solar cells, light-emitting diodes (LED), touch panels and _____.
e: Graphene is widely used for solar cells, LEDs, touch panels and smart windows or phones.

q: Activated charcoal is used as an adsorbent in industry for bleaching, deodourization and _____.
e: Activated charcoal is used for bleaching, deodourization and water purification.

q: Coke is used as a fuel in the metal industry and as a reducing agent in the extraction of metals such as _____.
e: Coke is used as a reducing agent in the extraction of lead, iron and zinc.

q: Carbon black is used for making printing ink, black shoes polish and as a filler in _____.
a: vehicle tyres and other rubber products
e: Carbon black is used as a filler in vehicle tyres and other rubber products.

q: Carbon is found in nature combined with other elements in petroleum, coal, natural gas, limestone, carbon dioxide and _____.
e: Carbon is found in compounds such as petroleum, coal, natural gas, limestone, carbon dioxide and sugar.

q: Carbon is a major component of giant molecules called macromolecules which include proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and _____.
e: Macromolecules include proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and carbohydrates.

q: Graphite is used in making _____ in the cells.
e: Graphite is used in making electrode in the cells.

q: Graphite crucibles are used as containers for _____ at high temperature.
e: Graphite crucibles are used as containers for melting metals at high temperature.

q: A very small amount of carbon is used to make some types of _____.
e: Carbon (very small amount) is used to make some types of steel.

q: Charcoal is commonly used as a fuel for _____.
e: Charcoal is used as a fuel for cooking.

q: Carbon black is used for making _____ and black shoes polish.
e: Carbon black is used for making printing ink and black shoes polish.

q: Halogens ($F_2$, $Cl_2$, $Br_2$, $I_2$) are _____ molecules.
e: Halogens are diatomic molecules.

q: At room temperature, fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a _____, and iodine is a solid.
e: Bromine is a liquid at room temperature.

q: The essential electronic structure of halogens is _____.
e: The essential electronic structure of halogen is $ns^2 np^5$.

q: Among the halogens, _____ is the most reactive.
e: Among them fluorine is the most reactive.

q: In nature, halogens are found as salts of the _____.
e: They are found as salts of the halides.

q: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and _____.
e: Halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated sulphuric acid.

q: Chlorine is collected by the upward displacement of air because it is slightly soluble in water and _____ than air.
e: It is collected by the upward displacement of air because it is slightly soluble in water and heavier than air.

q: Due to its _____ colour, chlorine gas can be seen easily when the gas jar is full.
e: Due to its greenish yellow colour, it can be seen easily.

q: If required dry, chlorine gas is passed into _____.
e: If required dry, the gas is passed into concentrated sulphuric acid.

q: The chemical equation for the preparation of chlorine is _____.
e: The equation is $2NaCl(s) + MnO_2(s) + 3H_2SO_4(l) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2NaHSO_4(aq) + MnSO_4(aq) + Cl_2(g) + 2H_2O(l)$.

q: Fluorine is a very _____ gas.
e: Fluorine is a very pale yellow gas.

q: Fluorine reacts with almost all other elements, except _____.
e: It reacts with almost all other elements, except helium and neon.

q: Chlorine is a _____ gas with a choking, unpleasant smell.
e: Chlorine is a pale green gas with a choking, unpleasant smell.

q: Chlorine is about _____ times as dense as air.
e: Chlorine is about 2.5 times as dense as air.

q: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, _____ liquid.
e: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, volatile liquid.

q: Bromine is slightly soluble in water, forming a _____ solution containing about 3 percent of bromine at ordinary temperature.
e: It forms a yellowish red solution containing about 3 percent of bromine.

q: Iodine is a _____ shiny solid with an irritating smell.
e: Iodine is a purple-black shiny solid and irritating smell.

q: Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a _____ vapour.
e: Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a violet vapour.

q: Iodine is almost insoluble in water but readily dissolves in aqueous potassium iodide to form a _____ solution.
e: This solution is brown due to the formation of a compound of potassium iodide and iodine.

q: Iodine dissolves in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride, forming _____ solutions.
e: Iodine forms violet solutions in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride.

q: The reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of _____.
e: Reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$.

q: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to sunlight, it _____.
e: When exposed to sunlight, it explodes.

q: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form _____.
e: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form metal chlorides.

q: When a very thin sheet of an alloy of copper and zinc is dropped into a chlorine gas jar, it burns brightly with a _____ flame.
e: It burns brightly with a green flame.

q: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine to form phosphorus(III) chloride and _____.
e: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine to form phosphorus(III) chloride and phosphorus(V) chloride.

q: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have bleaching power, however, _____ does not.
e: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have bleaching power, however, iodine does not.

q: Chlorine reacts with water to form HOCl and _____.
e: Chlorine reacts with water to form HOCl and HCl.

q: The HOCl slowly decomposes to hydrochloric acid and _____.
e: The HOCl slowly decomposes to hydrochloric acid and nascent oxygen.

q: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by _____ them.
e: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by oxidising them.

q: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. This is used as a test for _____.
e: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. This is used as a test for chlorine.

q: Halogens are _____ agents.
e: Halogens are oxidising agents.

q: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into _____.
e: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into iron(III) chloride.

q: Iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and liberate _____.
e: Iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and liberate sulphur.

q: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium hypochlorite and _____.
e: The products are potassium chloride, potassium hypochlorite and water.

q: Chlorine reacts with hot concentrated potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium chlorate and _____.
e: The products are potassium chloride, potassium chlorate and water.

q: When chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide, the respective halogen is displaced by more reactive chlorine to form sodium chloride and _____.
e: Chlorine displaces bromine to form sodium chloride and bromine.

q: When bromine is passed into a solution of sodium iodide, _____ is liberated.
e: Bromine displaces iodine, so iodine is liberated.

q: Iodine cannot displace chlorine and bromine from their salt solutions because it is _____ reactive.
e: Iodine is less reactive and cannot displace chlorine and bromine.

q: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a _____ charge.
e: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a negative charge.

q: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding _____ solution.
e: The presence of halide ions can be tested by adding silver nitrate solution.

q: Samples for the silver nitrate test are typically acidified with dilute nitric acid to remove interfering ions, e.g., _____ ions.
e: Acidified with dilute nitric acid to remove interfering ions, e.g., carbonate ions.

q: In the silver nitrate test for halides, different colours of _____ precipitates are observed.
e: Different colours of silver halides precipitates are observed.

q: Fluorine is used in the form of fluorides in drinking water to prevent tooth decay by hardening the _____ on teeth.
e: Fluorides prevent tooth decay by hardening the enamel on teeth.

q: Chlorine is used to make PVC (Polyvinyl chloride) plastic as well as household _____.
e: Chlorine is used to make PVC plastic as well as household bleaches.

q: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and _____.
e: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and fire retardants.

q: Iodine is used in medicines to treat cases of _____ and as a disinfectant (e.g., 'Tincture of iodine').
e: Iodine is used in medicines to treat cases of goiter.

q: Halides are widely used in metal halide lamps that are _____.
e: Halides are widely used in metal halide lamps that are high-intensity discharge lamps.
